messages:
sara: Heads up — prod-us-central1 is showing a weird mismatch: racks with 0.75 spare GPU capacity are idle but many tiny inference jobs are pending. This started ~45m ago.
matt: any recent scheduler or node-label changes?
sara: op: we rolled out `rack-preference=dedicated` labels to compute nodes yesterday as part of segregation work. Also bumped lease TTL to 10m during that rollout.
olivia: pasted `kubectl get pods -n prod | grep Pending` snippet (trimmed):
```
viz-infer-7    Pending   0/1 nodes are available: 1 node(s) didn't match node selector
mini-job-421   Pending   0/1 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate
```
devin: sounds like two problems: nodeSelector prevents tiny jobs from landing, + taint `gpu:rack=dedicated:NoSchedule` blocks them. Why did rollout add that taint?
sara: the taint is to prevent colocating large training jobs on certain racks. It was meant to apply only to `large` pools but selector scoping bug hit all GPU nodes.
infra-bot: ALERT: [gpu-pending-pods] cluster-prod-us-central1 threshold breached (count=78) at 1799800060
matt: autoscaler attempted scale-up but cloud returned `CapacityError: insufficientGpus`. Also note warm-pool nodes are not being filled because the scheduler refuses fractional coalescing since `coalesce_policy=strict` in config.
olivia: quick mitigation I applied: added a toleration to the tiny deployment templates and rolled a couple of pods. command used: `kubectl patch deploy mini-job -n prod --type=json -p='[{"op":"add","path":"/spec/template/spec/tolerations/-","value":{"key":"gpu:rack","operator":"Equal","value":"dedicated","effect":"NoSchedule"}}]'`
devin: good for immediate, but that mixes tiny inference into dedicated racks — expect bursty cross-az traffic and cost delta. Monitor egress.
matt: we can also toggle `allow_fractional_coalesce=true` for tiny workloads only. Safer approach: scheduler needs a per-class coalescing whitelist.
sara: rolled tolerations to 10% of tiny pods, pending dropped from 78 -> 21 in 9 minutes. Cost bump small (~6% for the rack) but acceptable short-term.
olivia: infra ticket CLOUD-9345 opened for label rollback and quota check. I've also escalated to cloud-ops for an emergency quota increase if autoscaler needs it.
devin: long-term fixes: 1) hotfix scheduler to honor `workload_class` for coalescing 2) add rollout gate: block taint/label changes if pending_gpus > 15 for 10m 3) reduce lease TTL back to 1m to speed rebalance 4) add a preflight check in CI so label changes auto-run a simulated packing check.
matt: also add a cheap heuristic: when warmpool_util < 50% and pending tiny pods > X, allow best-effort fractional packing across racks with a cost-rate cap.
sara: creating INFRA-2061 to track these action items + a runbook entry for on-call (rollback taint label, patch tolerations, scale provisioner). Adding owners: @matt (scheduler), @olivia (runbook), @devin (quota).
ops-bot: Incident INFRA-2061 created by sara at 1799800185.
infra-bot: RESOLVED ALERT: pending_gpus returned to 18 at 1799800198.
matt: follow-up: we need a canary around the label agent. Propose: 1) 5% node rollout 2) measure pending_gpu delta over 15m 3) abort if delta > 10. I'll open a PR for the agent.
devin: agree. I'll coordinate with cloud-ops to pre-check quotas before rollout and add fallback region mapping for non-latency-critical jobs.
olivia: leaving monitoring on. Will post postmortem in #eng-infra when INFRA-2061 is fleshed out. :thumbsup:
